Answer: D
Reason: The chest X-ray shows a small, hypoplastic left lung with ipsilateral mediastinal shift and compensatory hyperinflation of the right lung, which are classic radiographic features of hypogenetic lung syndrome (congenital pulmonary hypoplasia). This congenital anomaly explains the patient's history of recurrent infections and stridor, unlike the other options which present with different imaging patterns (e.g., hyperlucent lung in Swyer-James or lobar overinflation).
